body: Kalia, 'The Effects of Promoter Share Pledging on Stock Price Crash Risk and Financial Performance' (Journal of Advances in Management Research, 2024; Emerald; low citations as it is recent): 257 S&P BSE 500 companies, 2011-2020, with panel fixed-effects and an IV-2SLS design to address the fact that weak firms may pledge more. Higher promoter pledging was significantly associated with higher FUTURE stock-price crash risk (negative skewness, down-to-up volatility) and with weaker future financial performance (ROA/Tobin's q), robust to alternative proxies. The mechanism: pledging promoters have incentives to hide bad news to avoid margin calls, so bad news accumulates and is released in a crash, and the margin-call spiral (falling price -> top-up or invocation -> forced selling) amplifies it. A companion paper by the same author (Asian Journal of Economics and Banking, 2024) links pledging to lower dividend payouts in family firms. Replicated: in China, a large literature (for example Dou et al.; Li-Zhou-Yan) finds the same crash-risk link; Indian academic evidence is thin and single-author, but it matches our case record (Zee/Essel, ADAG, Future Group, CG Power, Jet). Use for us: keep pledge as a hard disqualifier above a threshold and as a sizing penalty below it. Rising pledge, pledges to NBFCs rather than banks, and pledges across several group companies are the worst versions; track them via the NSE pledge feed.

data.finding: pledge -> higher crash risk, lower performance

title: India: promoter share pledging predicts higher stock-price crash risk and weaker performance (Kalia 2024, BSE 500, 2011-2020)
